name: High-tech
summary: A lightweight steel frame, with the services, the bracing and the lifts shown in colour on the outside. Rogers, Piano and Foster made the machine aesthetic of the 1920s into a flexible, kit-of-parts building.

philosophy.core_thesis: A building is a machine of parts: structure, services and circulation are tools to see and to change, and open floors let the use change.
design_principles: Free the floor plate: span 12 to 48m with trusses or tension rods, so that the interior has no columns in the use area.
Put services outside, on the facade or the roof: ducts, pipes, lifts and stairs, coloured by function (blue air, green water, yellow power, red escape).
Build from a kit of prefabricated parts: steel members, pins, castings and glass panels that are bolted, not welded on site.
Show the joints: bolts, pins, cast gerberettes and tension rods are the detail that carries the elevation.
Wrap the frame in a thin skin of glass or metal panel, with a window-to-wall ratio of 60 to 100%.
Plan for change: a regular bay of 6 to 12m, a raised floor of 150 to 600mm, and walls that move.
anti_patterns: Services hidden in a ceiling void and a cladded riser
Welded smooth joints that hide how the part is fixed

massing.form: A clear rectangular box of 3 to 8 storeys, with the stairs, lifts and ducts in separate bands or towers beside it.
massing.proportion: Wide and low: 2:1 to 4:1 length to height; the long front is a screen of frame and glass.
massing.roof: A flat roof with plant, masts and tension-rod trusses; the roof edge is a thin line.
massing.relation_to_ground: A raised public plaza or a ground floor open on all sides, so that the building sits like a machine on a platform.

structure.system: A steel frame with trusses, tension members and cast steel joints, on a 6 to 12m module.
structure.span_and_module: Floor spans of 12 to 48m; the frame bay of 6 to 12.8m; floors are 3.5 to 4.2m storey to storey.
structure.expression: All members are visible, from the cross-bracing to the pins; the structure is the main decoration.

materials.finish: Factory-made and exact: paint in primary colours, brushed stainless, clear glass, and bolted joints.

facade.composition: A frame of columns, bracing and floors in front of glass, with a coloured layer of services and a glazed outside escalator or stair.
facade.openings: Full-height glazing; the window-to-wall ratio is 60 to 100%, with solid panels only at the cores.
facade.solid_to_void: Void leads: 0–40% opaque, mostly as steel members and panels.

light_and_space.daylight: Light reaches deep plans through full glass fronts, rooflights and atrium; the structure casts a fine line of shadow.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: A free open floor reached by a long glazed escalator or a lift on the outside; the plan is a field, not a sequence.
light_and_space.interior_character: Bare steel soffits, raised floors, movable partitions and visible services in the ceiling.

ornament.attitude: No applied ornament; the detail of the joint, the colour code of the services and the structure are the image.

emotion.target_response: Energy and openness: the viewer feels a machine that works in public and welcomes change.

avoid_when: The brief asks for domestic warmth, traditional craft or a heavy masonry building.
The site has strong rules on a historic roofline or a quiet street front.

modifiers.how: Replace the steel frame with cast concrete members of the same grid, show services in a concrete tower, and reduce the glazing to 40%.

sources.title: Colin Davies, High Tech Architecture (Thames & Hudson, 1988)
